title: Larkfield pilot call + integration sprint capture
content:
Meeting: Larkfield Supply — Pilot kickoff (2025-04-01)
Attendees: Elena (RDW CS), Jonas (RDW Solutions), Priya (RDW Eng), Mark Ross (Larkfield Head of Ops), Ana Gomez (Larkfield Platform), Dev Patel (Larkfield SRE)
Purpose: Clarify scope for 6-week pilot: conversational assistant for inbound carrier ETA questions + returns routing. Capture integration constraints, SLOs, and next steps.

Summary notes (rough)
- Business goal: reduce support ops time for ETA/return status queries by 40% and automate straightforward returns routing. Larkfield expects immediate UX improvement on web chat and internal Slack channel.
- Pilot scope: NLU + retrieval over: (1) tracking events table, (2) returns policy doc set, (3) last-30-days SKU-level delay history. No PII to be sent to hosted model.
- Deployment model: Larkfield prefers Private (VPC) deployment for initial pilot to keep event data inside network. They will consider Dedicated later.

Key technical constraints called out by Ana / Dev:
1) Network: Larkfield runs in AWS account A123. They require the control plane to be reachable only from specific egress IPs and only over mTLS. VPN/Transit gateway option acceptable.
2) Data residency: logs and request payloads must not leave VPC. Redwood needs to support KMS integration for encryption-at-rest.
3) Throughput: expected peak concurrent users ~80, average 20 qps for conversational queries during business hours. Typical request size small but retrieval vectors can be up to 8k tokens for long returns policy sections.
4) Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 500ms for direct slot-filling queries; up to 1.5s acceptable for retrieval+generation flows.
5) Embedding freshness: tracking events change rapidly — they want embeddings updated every 15 minutes for recent events.
6) Auth model: they use OAuth2 service account tokens; need short-lived signed JWTs for call routing.

Risks / gotchas identified on call
- Embedding churn: 15-minute cadence for vector refresh is aggressive and will increase write load and storage costs. Need to estimate cost and recommend either incremental upsert or time-windowed caching.
- Long documents: some returns policies are PDFs with tables. We need a preprocessor for table extraction and consistent chunking (keep table rows together).
- Token billing surprises: Larkfield's internal projections use naive token estimates. For 8k token contexts and streaming generation, cost can be 2–3x expected if left unbounded.
- Internal routing: Larkfield wants to fallback to a legacy FAQ service when confidence < 0.6. Need confidence scoring and a configurable fallback route.

Architecture decisions to validate
- Run Retrieval as a Redwood Private instance in their VPC with local vector DB (we proposed Pinecone-hosted but they insist on self-hosted). Verify compatible vector store (we recommend Milvus/FAISS on k8s).
- Use Redwood prefix/KV caching for repeated recent queries (helps event-heavy traffic). Cache TTL for tracking events should be 60s and support invalidation on new events.
- Model family: recommend a quantized Llama-3 variant for generation with a faster reranker (smaller encoder model) for shortlist. Must test latency in private environment.

Prompting / eval notes (quick raw thoughts)
- Primary prompt pattern: system: "You are LarkfieldOps assistant. Use only data from the docs and tracking table provided. If unsure, ask a clarifying question or fallback to FAQ." user: <customer query> retrieval: <top-5 passages>. Include a short source attribution line.
- Example test query: "Where is order #D9F-4412?" Expected resolved flow: identify order id => query tracking events => summarize latest events + estimated delivery window => if last event is >48h without movement, escalate (link to return/claims flow).
- Evaluation metrics: accuracy @1 (correct ETA) target 85% on synthetic test set, hallucination rate under 5% on policy answers, mean token cost per user < 150 tokens.

Short checklist (engineering)
- [ ] Provision Private cluster image and bootstrap script for Larkfield VPC (RDW infra)
- [ ] Create sample connector to Larkfield tracking API (Jonas) — schema mapping doc required
- [ ] Build ingestion pipeline for returns PDFs (Priya) — table extraction + chunking rules
- [ ] Prototype embedding refresh worker with incremental upserts every 15 minutes (Elena + Jonas)
- [ ] Implement confidence-based routing + fallback to FAQ endpoint (Dev)
- [ ] Run baseline latency/load test with quantized Llama-3 model image inside Larkfield VPC (SRE team)
- [ ] Cost estimate for 6-week pilot + 3-month steady state (Finance assist)

Assigned next steps (who, what, by when)
- Elena: draft pilot success criteria doc and share with Larkfield by 2025-04-04. Include the evaluation metrics and will ask for 200 synthetic queries from their ops team.
- Jonas: spike on tracking API connector and produce schema mapping and sample webhook flow by 2025-04-07. Put PR link under linked_artifacts.
- Priya: initial scraper for PDFs + table extraction proof-of-concept (fast prototype) by 2025-04-09. Test on 5 sample policy docs from Ana.
- Dev (Larkfield): set aside VPC subnet and open a ticket for RDW to request VPN credentials by 2025-04-06.
- SRE (RDW): schedule load test window in Larkfield VPC week of 2025-04-14. Need baseline model image and sample dataset from Jonas.

Open questions to clarify with Larkfield (action: Elena)
- Can Larkfield accept partial logs for debugging (sanitized) or do they require zero log export outside VPC? If partial allowed, we can ship better analytics.
- Confirm retention policy for embeddings and cached artifacts (30 days vs 90 days?).
- Clarify SSO flow for internal Slack integration: do they prefer app-level bot token or enterprise install?

Notes to self / sketch ideas
- Consider recommending hybrid embedding strategy: dense vectors for recent events (high churn) updated frequently, and sparser summary embeddings for older events updated daily. Reduces write pressure.
- For tables, use a 2-step chunk: (1) table row level embedding for precise lookup, (2) table-level summary for natural-language summary generation.
- Precompute "short answers" templates for common ETA responses to cap token usage. Use small prefix model for templating + generator for nuance.

Meeting artifacts to attach later
- sample-tracking-schema.csv (Jonas)
- returns-policy-samples.zip (Ana)
- pilot-eval-queries.xlsx (ops)

Quick raw timeline
- Week 1 (2025-04-07): connector + ingestion POC, infra provisioning started
- Week 2–3: embedding pipeline, confidence fallback, basic UI integration in web chat
- Week 4: internal QA + cost run, revise chunking/embedding cadence
- Week 5: invite ops users for pilot, collect synthetic queries, iterate prompts
- Week 6: measure metrics, decision point on Dedicated vs continue Private

Bottom line (for execs): Larkfield is a good fit for a Private pilot but expect effort on embedding freshness and table handling. Short-term wins: immediate reduction in simple ETA queries via caching + templated short answers. Longer term: adoption depends on cost per query after embedding cadence and whether they accept some sanitized logging for ops visibility.

-- End scratchpad.

Rough tags for search: larkfield pilot, private deployment, embedding cadence, returns policy extraction, ETA assistant
